topic.title: The Two-Cent Bottleneck: Are Sold-Out MLCC Ceramic Capacitors Quietly Constraining AI Server Production?
topic.trigger: DigiTimes reported September 14, 2026 that AI servers are consuming a growing share of global MLCC (multilayer ceramic capacitor) capacity and that Chinese suppliers are absorbing spillover demand, following Samsung Electro-Mechanics' 30% MLCC price increase (effective August 1, 2026) and Murata's 15-35% price increase (effective April 1, 2026), plus record Q1/Q2 2026 earnings at both companies driven by data-center demand.

questions.primary: Have AI-server-grade high-capacitance MLCC ceramic capacitors become a genuine structural bottleneck on AI accelerator production, distinct from the chip, memory, packaging and power-equipment constraints this pipeline has previously examined?
sub: How concentrated is AI-server-grade MLCC supply, and how fast can that capacity expand?
What is driving MLCC demand growth specifically from AI servers versus other end markets?
Is there a credible near-term substitute for high-capacitance MLCCs in AI server power-delivery networks?
How does the current MLCC tightness compare to the industry's historical 2018-2019 shortage-to-glut cycle?
Could Chinese MLCC manufacturers or next-generation capacitor technologies meaningfully ease the constraint before 2027?

thesis: A near-duopoly of Murata Manufacturing and Samsung Electro-Mechanics, controlling an estimated 84% of AI-server-grade high-capacitance MLCC (multilayer ceramic capacitor) supply, is running production at 90-95% utilization with 12-24 month lead times to add qualified new capacity, while AI servers built on Nvidia's GB300 platform consume an estimated 10-15x more MLCCs than a general-purpose server. Both leading suppliers posted record 2026 earnings, imposed successive double-digit price increases, and are steering new capacity toward long-term hyperscaler contracts -- evidence that this unglamorous multi-cent passive component meets the strict Structural Bottleneck test even though it receives far less market attention than HBM memory, advanced packaging or grid equipment. Its durability is more contested than most of this pipeline's prior findings: the MLCC industry has a well-documented history of whipsawing from acute shortage to oversupply within about 18 months, Chinese manufacturers and complementary technologies (silicon capacitors, polymer tantalum) are already scaling into the gap, and next-generation platforms like Nvidia's Vera Rubin could either extend or -- if paired with faster capacity delivery -- help close the shortfall.

facts.statement: Murata Manufacturing's Q1 FY2026 (April-June 2026) revenue reached a record 502.3 billion yen, up 20.7% year-over-year, driven mainly by data-center and mobility demand; the MLCC business's book-to-bill ratio reached 1.47x in the quarter.

Murata plans approximately 80 billion yen in additional MLCC capacity investment (about 40 billion yen in each of FY2026 and FY2027), focused on small-form-factor, high-capacitance specifications, but expects total capacity to increase only 10-15% from current levels once the investment is complete.
Murata notified customers in March 2026 of a 15-35% price increase on AI-server-grade and automotive-grade MLCCs, effective April 1, 2026.

Samsung Electro-Mechanics reported Q2 2026 (April-June) consolidated sales of 3,457.2 billion Korean won and operating profit of 440.4 billion won, up 107% year-over-year and 57% quarter-over-quarter; MLCC revenue grew 44% year-over-year and 19% quarter-over-quarter, and operating margin improved to 12.7% from 7.6% a year earlier.
As of its Q2 2026 report, Samsung Electro-Mechanics had signed long-term MLCC supply contracts with more than 10 customers, including hyperscalers and major semiconductor companies.

Samsung Electro-Mechanics notified sales partners on July 29, 2026 of a 30% price increase across its MLCC product portfolio, effective August 1, 2026, citing structural growth in global electronics demand outpacing what the supply chain can absorb.
TrendForce reported on August 18, 2026 that high-end MLCC lead times have diverged to 5-10 months and that tightness may extend into 2027.

TrendForce reported on August 4, 2026 an across-the-board MLCC price surge of roughly 30%, following Samsung Electro-Mechanics' price action and reports that Taiyo Yuden was considering a similar increase effective September 1, 2026.

DigiTimes reported on September 14, 2026 that Murata holds an estimated 45% and Samsung Electro-Mechanics an estimated 39% share of the AI-server-grade (high-capacitance, low-ESL) MLCC market, a combined 84%, and that Chinese suppliers are absorbing overflow demand these two companies cannot fill.

TrendForce reported on June 17, 2026 that cloud service providers' in-house custom-ASIC programs are concentrating demand on a narrower set of high-end MLCC specifications, and flagged a risk of structural shortages in high-end specialty MLCCs emerging in the second half of 2026.

Samsung Electro-Mechanics announced in May 2026 a silicon-capacitor supply contract worth approximately $1 billion with a major global customer, covering deliveries through 2027-2028; industry analysis frames silicon capacitors as complementary to, not a substitute for, MLCCs in AI-server power-delivery networks.

Nvidia has publicly announced its Vera Rubin AI platform as the successor to its current Blackwell/GB300 generation, positioned to scale AI-factory power density and rack-level system complexity substantially beyond current deployments.

The global MLCC industry experienced a severe supply shortage from early 2018 through mid-2019, driven by automotive and consumer-electronics demand growth outpacing capacity, which was followed by a rapid swing to oversupply and price erosion beginning in the second half of 2019 as double-ordered inventory was cancelled.

Chinese MLCC manufacturers -- including Guangdong Fenghua Advanced Technology and Chaozhou Three-Circle (Sanhuan Group) -- reported robust orders and high capacity utilization through mid-2026, with Fenghua implementing two price increases in 2026 totaling roughly 20%, while combined Chinese makers' global MLCC market share is reported to have risen to roughly 10%, up from about 6% in 2019.

inferences.statement: The combination of 90-95% reported utilization at the two leading AI-server-grade MLCC makers, 12-24 month lead times to bring new qualified high-capacitance capacity online, and successive double-digit price increases across essentially all major suppliers in 2026 indicates this segment currently meets the strict Structural Bottleneck test (extreme demand growth, low supply elasticity, hard substitutability) at least through 2027.

Because Murata and Samsung Electro-Mechanics together hold an estimated 84% share of AI-server-grade MLCC supply and are directing new capacity primarily toward long-term contracted hyperscaler and semiconductor customers, AI-server builders without such contracts likely face materially longer effective allocation delays than the headline 5-10 month lead-time figures suggest.

Next-generation AI accelerator platforms such as Nvidia's Vera Rubin are likely to increase per-rack MLCC and capacitor consumption meaningfully beyond current GB300-generation levels, given reported increases in power density and rack-level energy storage, which would extend rather than relieve AI-driven demand pressure into 2027-2028; however, the specific magnitude cited in trade press (up to several hundred thousand units per rack) is a third-party estimate, not a figure Nvidia has disclosed.

Because MLCC shortages have historically proven cyclical rather than permanent -- the 2018-2019 episode reversed within roughly 18 months once double-ordered inventory unwound -- the current AI-driven tightness carries a meaningful risk of a comparable correction once hyperscaler capex growth decelerates or the 2027 capacity additions from Murata, Samsung Electro-Mechanics and Chinese entrants land simultaneously.

Partial substitution paths already being commercially deployed -- silicon capacitors for certain power-delivery functions and polymer tantalum capacitors for bulk decoupling -- may cap the ceiling on MLCC price increases and lead-time extension compared with bottlenecks that have no substitution path at all, such as ASML's EUV lithography monopoly examined in this pipeline's September 9, 2026 report.

unknowns: The precise current lead time and allocation status of AI-server-grade MLCCs for AI system integrators that lack long-term contracts (versus the headline hyperscaler-contracted lead times) is not independently disclosed by Murata or Samsung Electro-Mechanics.

Whether any hyperscaler or AI server OEM has publicly disclosed a production delay or shipment slip specifically attributed to MLCC or passive-component unavailability -- as opposed to GPU, HBM, or power-equipment constraints -- is unconfirmed in available sources.

The exact MLCC count and specification requirements for Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform have not been officially disclosed by Nvidia; currently circulating figures are third-party trade-press estimates of uncertain reliability.
Whether Chinese MLCC makers will achieve AI-server-grade qualification at meaningful volume before the 2027 capacity additions from Murata and Samsung Electro-Mechanics come online is unknown.

bottlenecks.node: AI-server-grade high-capacitance MLCC fabrication (Murata / Samsung Electro-Mechanics duopoly)
bottlenecks.rationale: Meets all three strict criteria: demand growth is Extreme (a single AI server is reported to require an order of magnitude more MLCCs than a general-purpose server, and both leading suppliers posted record profit growth on data-center demand); supply elasticity is Low (90-95% utilization, 12-24 month capacity lead times, and Murata's own ~80 billion yen investment adds only 10-15% capacity); and substitutability is Hard for the specific high-capacitance, low-ESL specifications AI power-delivery networks require, since silicon capacitors and polymer tantalum capacitors are documented as complementary rather than full replacements.

bottlenecks.node: Barium titanate ceramic powder and nickel/palladium electrode materials
bottlenecks.rationale: Raw-material cost pressure (ceramic powder and electrode metals) is contributing to MLCC price increases, but available evidence shows cost pass-through rather than a proven physical supply constraint independent of MLCC fabrication capacity itself, so it does not meet the strict Low-supply-elasticity/Hard-substitutability bar on its own.

Chinese makers are scaling capacity and gaining share, functioning as a partial release valve for the broader MLCC market, but they are reported to still trail Murata and Samsung Electro-Mechanics in the dielectric thickness, layer count and long-term reliability data needed for top-tier AI-server qualification, so they do not yet resolve the binding constraint at the highest specification tier.

companies.revenue_model: Component sales under a mix of spot and long-term supply agreements.

Murata's ~80 billion yen capacity expansion completing across FY2026-FY2027

bear_case.argument: The MLCC industry has a well-documented history of whipsawing from acute shortage to oversupply within about 18 months, as occurred in 2018-2019 once double-ordered inventory was cancelled; the same dynamic could unwind the current AI-driven tightness faster than the 2027-2028 capacity timeline suggests.

Silicon capacitors and polymer tantalum capacitors are already being commercially deployed in AI-server power-delivery networks, providing a partial substitution path that pure structural bottlenecks like EUV lithography lack.

Chinese MLCC makers have already lifted combined global share from about 6% (2019) to roughly 10% and are actively pursuing AI-server qualification, adding incremental supply that could erode the Murata/Samsung Electro-Mechanics duopoly's pricing power sooner than expected.

Because MLCC demand growth is a direct derivative of hyperscaler AI accelerator shipment volumes, any deceleration in aggregate hyperscaler capital-expenditure guidance -- a risk flagged across nearly every report in this pipeline -- would flow through directly to MLCC order books and book-to-bill ratios.

Both Murata and Samsung Electro-Mechanics are simultaneously investing in new capacity (Murata's ~80 billion yen plan; Samsung Electro-Mechanics' undisclosed but implied expansion funding its 10+ long-term contracts); if these land concurrently with a Chinese capacity wave in 2027, supply could overshoot even continued AI demand growth.
